title: Voltage Sources vs. Current Sources
description: Voltage and Current Sources - Comparison and characteristics of voltage sources and current sources in electrical circuits

rows: Maintains a fixed supply voltage independent of circuit load resistance and applied current
Maintains a fixed supply current independent of circuit load resistance and applied voltage
Voltage remains constant regardless of load
Current remains constant regardless of load
Prefers open circuits (no connection between poles)

components.content:
## Key Differences

### Voltage Source
* Maintains a **fixed supply voltage** to an electrical circuit
* Voltage is independent of the circuit load resistance and the applied current
* Real voltage and current sources have limits to the voltage/currents they can provide
* A voltage source "prefer" open circuits (no connection between the poles)

### Current Source
* Maintains a **fixed supply current** through an electric circuit
* Current is independent of the circuit load resistance and applied voltage
* Real voltage and current sources have limits to the voltage/currents they can provide
* Current sources "prefer" closed circuits (short cuts)
